## Natural history notes

A large assassin bug characterized by its gray-brown body, long legs, piercing beak, and distinctive cogwheel-like crest rising from the back of the thorax. In Florida, the North American Wheel Bug is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, hammocks, parks, yards, and wooded or shrubby areas where insect prey is abundant. It is a beneficial predator that stalks caterpillars, beetles, flies, and other insects, stabbing them with its beak and injecting digestive saliva, but it should not be handled because its defensive bite can be very painful.
